answer: Sybil resistance arises because coordinated equivocation is treated as correlated misconduct: when k identities sign conflicting states, the bonded collateral penalty grows as O(k²), making larger collusions disproportionately expensive. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the controlled swarm, so hidden coordination rapidly destroys economic stake. Thus, an attacker cannot cheaply scale identities; every echo across the cedar network exposes links, while the meadow of apparent agents becomes a liability.
